Please solve this issue: Writebook lets an editor drop images straight into a page's markdown body:
each image is uploaded once and then referenced inline from the page's
content. Delete that page, and the image never actually leaves the app — the
file survives on disk, and the record that tracks it survives in the
database, forever, even once any background work the deletion sets off has
finished running. We cleared out a batch of stale pages and the storage bill
barely moved.

Fix it so that after a page whose markdown has an embedded image is destroyed,
and once any background work that destruction triggers has run to completion,
neither the image's file nor the record tracking it exists anywhere in the app.

Uploading a new image into a page's markdown, and then fetching that image back
from the URL the app hands you for it, has to keep working exactly as it does
today.

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class ReproEdgeTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActiveJob::TestHelper

  def upload(markdown, name = "reading.webp")
    markdown.uploads.attach(io: File.open(Rails.root.join("test/fixtures/files/#{name}")), filename: name, content_type: "image/webp")
    markdown.uploads.attachments.last
  end

  test "trashed page's image is purged when the page is destroyed" do
    leaf = leaves(:welcome_page)
    att = upload(leaf.leafable.body.tap(&:save!))
    blob = att.blob
    leaf.trashed!
    leaf.destroy!
    perform_enqueued_jobs
    assert_not ActiveStorage::Attachment.exists?(att.id)
    assert_not ActiveStorage::Blob.exists?(blob.id)
    assert_not blob.service.exist?(blob.key)
  end

  test "multiple revisions with several uploads are all purged on destroy" do
    leaf = leaves(:welcome_page)
    a1 = upload(leaf.leafable.body.tap(&:save!))
    travel 1.hour { leaf.edit leafable_params: { body: "v2 ![a](#{a1.slug_path})" } }
    a2 = upload(leaf.reload.leafable.body.tap(&:save!), "white-rabbit.webp")
    travel 1.hour { leaf.edit leafable_params: { body: "v3 ![b](#{a2.slug_path})" } }
    assert_equal 2, leaf.edits.revision.count
    blobs = [a1.blob, a2.blob]
    keys = blobs.map(&:key)
    service = blobs.first.service

    leaf.destroy!
    perform_enqueued_jobs

    assert_equal 0, ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(id: [a1.id, a2.id]).count
    assert_equal 0, ActiveStorage::Blob.where(id: blobs.map(&:id)).count
    keys.each { |k| assert_not service.exist?(k) }
    assert_equal 0, Page.where(id: [leaf.leafable_id]).count
  end

  test "an edit alone does not purge an image that the current page still references" do
    leaf = leaves(:welcome_page)
    att = upload(leaf.leafable.body.tap(&:save!))
    blob = att.blob
    travel 1.hour { leaf.edit leafable_params: { body: "changed ![x](#{att.slug_path})" } }
    perform_enqueued_jobs

    assert ActiveStorage::Blob.exists?(blob.id)
    assert blob.service.exist?(blob.key)
    assert ActiveStorage::Attachment.exists?(att.id)
  end

    perform_enqueued_jobs

    assert_not ActiveStorage::Blob.exists?(blob.id)
    assert_equal 0, ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(blob_id: blob.id).count
  end
end

    assert_not ActiveStorage::Blob.exists?(blob.id)

    keys = blobs.map(&:key)
    service = blobs.first.service

    perform_enqueued_jobs

      leaf.edit leafable_params: { body: "changed ![x](#{att.slug_path})" }
    end
    perform_enqueued_jobs

    assert_equal 1, leaf.edits.revision.count
    assert ActiveStorage::Blob.exists?(blob.id)
    assert blob.service.exist?(blob.key)

    perform_enqueued_jobs

    assert_not ActiveStorage::Blob.exists?(blob.id)
    assert_equal 0, ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(blob_id: blob.id).count
  end
end

messages.content:
Deleting a page with an embedded image now removes the attachment, the blob record, and the file, once the purge job has run. Uploading and fetching images is unchanged.

There were two separate causes:

1. **The image was never purged.** `ActionText::Markdown` declared `has_many_attached :uploads, dependent: :destroy`. That destroys the attachment row but never purges the blob, since Active Storage only does that when the option is `:purge_later`. I changed it to `dependent: :purge_later` in `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb`.

2. **Images uploaded before an edit survived.** Editing a page stores the old version as a revision that owns the old markdown, and the uploads stay attached to it. `Leaf` removed revisions with `has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all`, which skips destroying the old pages. I changed it to `dependent: :destroy` in `app/models/leaf/editable.rb`, so revisions and their uploads are cleaned up too. The tradeoff is that deleting a leaf with a long edit history now runs callbacks for each revision, not one `DELETE`.

**Verification**
- I reproduced the original bug first: after destroying the page and running the jobs, the blob record and file were still there.
- I added four tests: a page destroy, a page with a revision, a picture revision sharing its blob with the current picture, and an end-to-end upload → fetch → destroy → 404 test in the uploads controller. All four fail on the original code and pass with the fix.
- Full suite: 183 runs, 0 failures. The 2 skips are pre-existing system tests. Rubocop is clean.

The purge runs through the same `purge_later` path that book covers and pictures already use, so the production worker setup needs no changes.
